The first rainfall sweeps across the new land in a glittering curtain, the long-dead dust drinking it in as the watching settlement cheers.
A new ocean finishes filling a great basin, its surface catching the dawn, raw coastlines greening at its edge for the very first time.
An atmosphere-processor ignites in a towering plume of cloud, its roar rolling across the plains as the distant settlement lights flicker in celebration.
A forest of seeded pines reaches the ridgeline at last, the high ground turning green as morning light breaks across the canopy below.
The first river finds the sea, carving its final miles through new delta mud, its water bright and cold under an unfamiliar sky.
A flock of seeded birds rises from the valley in a wheeling mass, their calls echoing across terrain that has never known birdsong before.
Ice at the polar shelf begins its long melt, cold streams threading south into the waiting lowlands, pooling into a lake by afternoon.
A storm breaks and clears, and for the first time the colonists see an honest blue sky stretching from horizon to horizon above them.
The first harvest is brought in under a low sun, the fields heavy with grain, a rainbow arching over the processing dome behind them.
A green dawn breaks across the new world, the horizon edged with the first true vegetation, the air carrying something almost like morning dew.
The pressure gauges finally read breathable, and a single technician steps outside without a helmet, standing in the open air, eyes wide and quiet.
Lightning strikes the high mesa in a brilliant flash and the thunder that follows rolls across open land for the first time in millennia.
A new lake fills a crater basin, its surface still and reflective, catching the stars on its first untroubled night as a living body of water.
Seed drones complete their final pass over the southern continent, releasing their payload into warm wind, the last quadrant of bare ground now planted.
The first clouds form naturally above the warming plains, rising without machine help, a sign the water cycle has learned to sustain itself alone.
A whale-analogue breaches in the new ocean for the first time, its great body catching the light before it falls back into the blue.
Coral structures begin forming along the shallow shelf, slow and patient, building the first reef this world has ever known from its own chemistry.
The carbon reading crosses the threshold and an alarm sounds, but it is the good alarm, the one they have waited years to hear.
Two separate forest fronts meet on the central plain, their canopies touching, the continent's great green belt finally joined from coast to coast.
A child born on the world steps outside for the first time without a suit, arms raised, laughing at the wind on her skin.
The magnetosphere strengthens enough to paint the first aurora across the polar sky, and the whole settlement comes out to watch in silence together.
Pollinators released six seasons ago are spotted in the eastern meadows, their populations self-sustaining now, moving unhurried between the flowers the project planted.
Snow falls on the high peaks for the first time and does not melt, the mountains wearing white through winter as they always should have.
A soil sample returns full of living organisms, the underground world finally awake, the deep network of fungi threading unseen beneath the greening surface.
The last atmosphere-processor shuts down, its work complete, its tower going dark and quiet as the world breathes on without any help at all.
